title: feat(drivers,spec)!: `GroupByNode.alias` is honoured by the three SQL faces (#6401)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6401

## The fact, re-verified on `e120a5a`

`GroupByNodeSchema` declares `alias` ("Alias for the projected group value",
defaulting to `field`). One execution path read it:

| Face | reads `alias`? |
|---|---|
| `objectql` in-memory fallback | ✅ `g.alias ?? g.field` |
| `driver-memory` | ✅ `normalizeGroupBy`, `memory-driver.ts:1068` — **not in the issue's table** |
| chart category resolver | ✅ `chartAggregateCategoryKey`, `alias ?? field` — **not in the issue's table** |
| `driver-sql` | ❌ both limbs `g.field` |
| `driver-turso` local + remote | ❌ |
| `driver-sqlite-wasm` | ❌ (inherits) |
| `driver-mongodb` | ❌ — cannot take a structured node at all |

So one aggregate returned rows keyed `closed_at` under pushdown and `qtr` under
the fallback, decided by `engine.ts`'s
`allStructuredSupported && !tzRequiresInMemory` — a driver capability bit and a
`timezone`, neither visible to the caller.

## Step one was a measurement, and it chose the leg

**Real non-test producers of `GroupByNode.alias`: ZERO.** Nothing in
`examples/` (showcase, CRM, todo — the showcase's `ObjectChart` uses the bare
string form), nothing in `apps/`, nothing in non-test `packages/`. Writers are
4 test sites plus 4 *declaring* surfaces (`query.zod.ts`, `chart.zod.ts`,
`mcp-http-tools.ts`, and the chart `strictObject` alias map that steers `as` /
`label` → `alias`).

Zero producers reads like "remove" — but ADR-0049's table does not split on
producers, it splits on **whether the feature exists**: a dangling promise is
removed, a live one with a missing gate is enforced. `alias` is live on three
consumers, and decisively it is **compelled by the publish gate** —
`validate-react-page-props.ts:491` errors `REACT_CHART_AXIS_UNKNOWN` unless a
chart's category axis is bound to `alias ?? field`, and tells the author in so
many words to "bind it to" the alias. A key the build gate makes you write is
not dangling. (Its error text meanwhile claims rows are "keyed by the RAW FIELD
NAMES" — the gate and the SQL faces contradicted each other.)

The zero-producer count is what makes enforcing **safe**, not what argues
against it: no shipped payload changes its result keys.

## What changed — every face, or none

- **`driver-sql`** — both limbs project `alias ?? field`; `?? as ??` only when
  the name actually moves. `presentedOutput` re-keyed by the OUTPUT column,
  matching the aggregation branch beside it (an aliased group value went
  unpresented before).
- **`driver-turso` REMOTE** — `"field" AS "alias"`; the alias reaches the
  statement as a quoted identifier and is therefore held to
  `assertSafeIdentifier`, like `field`.
- **`driver-sqlite-wasm`** — inherits, covered by its own suite.

**GROUP BY still keys on the FIELD** on every face — pinned, because SQLite
resolves output names in `GROUP BY` and a face that grouped by the alias would
look correct on SQLite and diverge elsewhere. `having` needed no change:
`applyHaving` filters on the aggregated row's own keys, so it follows the
projection and now means one thing on every path.

## Conformance

`AGGREGATION_CASES` gains a `groupByAlias` axis + 2 cases whose VALUES are an
existing case verbatim — they can fail only on the KEY. `objectql`'s in-memory
fallback is **enrolled** as a fourth face (#6409 open question ②): it is the
face the SQL three were converged onto, and `applyInMemoryAggregation` turned
out to be a pure function of rows, so no engine was needed.

## Reverse verification — predicted before running

| Direction | Predicted | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| **A** pre-fix state | 1 fail on the named case per SQL face; degenerate `alias === field` green | ✅ `driver-sql` 1/18, `driver-turso` 3/34, `sqlite-wasm` 1/15, `objectql` 0 |
| **B** group by the alias (copied neighbour) | values blind; only the emitted-SQL pin catches it | ✅ `driver-sql` 18/18 and wasm 15/15 **green**; turso fails on `GROUP BY "bucket"` |
| **C** harness reads `c.groupBy` | all green (false GREEN) | ❌ **prediction wrong** — 1 fail per face |

Two results recorded rather than tidied away:

- **(C) was wrong.** Reading the field name against a face that *honours* the
  alias fails loudly. The false green needs **both** mistakes together, measured
  directly: face reverted + harness reading the field name = **18/18 green**.
- **`driver-sqlite-wasm`'s suite consumes `driver-sql`'s built `dist`**, not its
  `src`, so direction A showed a spurious 15/15 green until `driver-sql` was
  rebuilt. That suite checks its inheritance at BUILD granularity.

## Frozen drivers (#5499) — measured, never flipped

- **`driver-memory`**: **agrees**. It already returned
  `{ field, alias: node.alias ?? node.field }` — it had reached the enforce
  answer independently, so no mechanical alignment was needed.
- **`driver-mongodb`**: DEBT, and **wider than alias**. `buildAggregationPipeline`
  types `groupBy` as `string[]` and builds `groupId[field] = '$' + field`, so a
  structured node — aliased or not — becomes the literal key `"[object Object]"`.
  The alias is unreachable rather than ignored. `mongodb-driver.ts:512` passes
  `(query as any).groupBy`, which is why `tsc` never saw it. Home: #6814.

## Tests & gates

- Faces: `objectql` 2685, `driver-sql` 1097, `driver-turso` 906,
  `driver-sqlite-wasm` 304 — all green. `spec` 8877, `lint` 1730,
  `driver-memory` 540, `driver-mongodb` 220 — green.
- **`lint.yml` gates: 59/59**, run step by step with exit statuses read
  directly. That includes the three workspace-wide `turbo run build` /
  `turbo run typecheck` steps that are *not* `check:*` scripts — the omission
  that took #6409 red in CI — plus `examples`/`downstream-contract` typechecks,
  and the `check:i18n*` pair run against a built workspace.

Changeset included; no `content/docs/releases/` edits.
